definitions.explanation: Lacking a regular pattern or consistency. Often used as a な-adjective to describe schedules, habits, or patterns that are not consistent.

examples.japanese: {不規則|ふきそく}な{生活|せいかつ}はよくない。
examples.english: An irregular lifestyle is not good for you.

examples.japanese: {不規則|ふきそく}{動詞|どうし}を{覚|おぼ}えるのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
{睡眠|すいみん}が{不規則|ふきそく}になると{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}しやすい。
examples.english: When your sleep becomes irregular, it's easy to get out of shape health-wise.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
Used as a な-adjective ({不規則|ふきそく}な) or as a noun. The opposite is {規則的|きそくてき} (regular, systematic) or {規則正|きそくただ}しい (orderly, regular).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不規則|ふきそく}な{生活|せいかつ} (irregular lifestyle)
- {不規則|ふきそく}{動詞|どうし} (irregular verb)
- {不規則|ふきそく}な{食事|しょくじ} (irregular meals)
- {不規則|ふきそく}な{勤務|きんむ} (irregular work hours)
